## 1. Purpose and scope

This report frames the facility's process-safety key performance indicators for Q2 on the API RP 754 four-tier model (KB-STD-API-RP-754): Tier-1 and Tier-2 Process Safety Events (lagging), and Tier-3 and Tier-4 leading indicators. Every count in this report is structured from the facts supplied in the facility's PSE event log; no count, rate, threshold, or benchmark has been generated where the underlying data was not supplied — such items are recorded as [GAP] entries and carried into the action plan in Section 8.

This report covers the **process-safety metric family only**. It is distinct from the occupational injury-rate family (TRIR / LTIFR / DART). The 12 recordable injuries noted in the source log are acknowledged in Section 7 and routed to the occupational workstream; they are **not** process safety events and are excluded from every PSE count and rate in this report.

## 2. Data protection statement

This report identifies contributors and owners by role label only (Shift Lead; Process Engineer; and the action owners in Section 8). It contains no personal name, government identifier, contact detail, address, date of birth, or medical detail, and it embeds no re-identification key or name-to-label mapping. Per the source log, the re-identification key is held in a separate access-controlled artifact; it must remain stored apart from this document. Occupational injury data appears only as an aggregate total (12 recordables); no injury sub-category is published in this report, and the source log's suppression of cells below five individuals (with secondary suppression) is preserved by not reproducing any sub-category breakdown here.

## 4. Lagging indicators — Tier-1 and Tier-2 Process Safety Events

### 4.1 KPI table — Q2

| Indicator | Definition basis | Count (Q2) | Rate formula (per 200,000 hours) | Rate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier-1 PSE count | KB-STD-API-RP-754 tier definitions | **3** (flange releases, as logged by the facility) | — | — | Count reported from facility log |
| Tier-1 PSE rate | KB-STD-API-RP-754 rate basis | 3 | (3 × 200,000) ÷ **[GAP: total Q2 work hours]** | **[GAP]** | **Not computable — fail-loud.** The denominator was not supplied; the rate is not estimated. |
| Tier-2 PSE count | KB-STD-API-RP-754 tier definitions | **[GAP]** | — | — | The log records no Tier-2 events, but does not state whether Tier-2 screening was performed. Absence of a record is not evidence of zero; see action A3. |
| Tier-2 PSE rate | KB-STD-API-RP-754 rate basis | [GAP] | ([GAP] × 200,000) ÷ [GAP: total Q2 work hours] | **[GAP]** | Not computable — both count confirmation and denominator outstanding |

**Denominator discipline (load-bearing):** the Tier-1 rate is *deliberately* reported as [GAP] rather than estimated. A fabricated or assumed hours figure would produce a rate that looks authoritative but is indefensible. The count of 3 stands on its own and is reported regardless. Once the facility supplies total Q2 work hours (action A1), the rate computes directly from the formula shown above.

### 4.2 Tier-1 classification — verification caveat

Under KB-STD-API-RP-754, assigning an event to Tier 1 (versus Tier 2, or below the reporting threshold) is a threshold test on the event facts — the material involved, the quantity released, and the consequence. The event log supplies the event type ("flange release") and the count (3) but **none of the per-event threshold-test facts**:

| Event | Material | Quantity released | Consequence | Tier evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flange release 1 | [GAP] | [GAP] | [GAP] | Tier-1 designation carried as reported by the facility — unverified |
| Flange release 2 | [GAP] | [GAP] | [GAP] | Tier-1 designation carried as reported by the facility — unverified |
| Flange release 3 | [GAP] | [GAP] | [GAP] | Tier-1 designation carried as reported by the facility — unverified |

The Tier-1 count of 3 is therefore reported **as classified by the facility**, with the classification evidence outstanding (action A2). If verification against the KB-STD-API-RP-754 tier definitions re-tiers any event, this report must be re-issued with the corrected counts.

### 4.3 Signal in the event pattern

Three loss-of-primary-containment events of the **same mechanism (flange release) in one quarter** is a repeat-mode signal that warrants a joint-integrity review, independent of the KPI arithmetic. Any resulting controls must follow the hierarchy of controls (KB-SNIP-HOC): prioritize elimination and engineering measures — for example, flange-joint integrity management, controlled-bolting practice, and gasket/joint specification review — over administrative reminders, and never rely on PPE-only treatments without documented justification. This report recommends the review (action A7); it does not pre-judge its findings, because the per-event facts are [GAP].

## 5. Leading indicators — Tier-3 and Tier-4

No leading-indicator data was supplied for Q2; both tiers are reported as [GAP] rather than zero. A healthy API RP 754 dashboard reports leading and lagging tiers together — the leading tiers are where deteriorating barrier health becomes visible *before* a Tier-1/Tier-2 event.

| Tier | What it measures (KB-STD-API-RP-754 framing) | Candidate indicators for this facility | Q2 value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 3 | Challenges to safety systems | Safety-instrumented-system demands; relief-device activations; safe-operating-limit excursions | **[GAP] — not tracked or not supplied** (action A4) |
| Tier 4 | Operating discipline and management-system performance | Procedure compliance; training currency; overdue inspections (including flange-joint / mechanical-integrity inspection backlog, given Section 4.3) | **[GAP] — not tracked or not supplied** (action A5) |

The candidate indicators above are the standard indicator families named in this skill's intake scope; the facility should confirm which it already measures before adopting the set.

## 6. Targets, thresholds, and RAG status

**A count only becomes a managed KPI once it carries a target or threshold.** No target, threshold, or red/amber/green band was supplied for any indicator, so **no RAG status is assigned in this report** — assigning one against an invented threshold would be fabrication. [GAP: per-indicator thresholds.]

Recommended mechanism (action A6): once the work-hours denominator and at least one prior period are available, the site should set red/amber/green bands per indicator against its own baseline and adopt them in the site KPI review. No numeric threshold is proposed here because no baseline data was supplied.

**Interpretation caution for the eventual rate:** a single-quarter rate built on a count of 3 is volatile — small changes in count or hours move it substantially. Read it alongside a multi-period trend (this report is single-period; prior-period data was not supplied) rather than as a standalone verdict.

## 7. Benchmarking and routing of occupational data

**Benchmark:** none was supplied, and no benchmark figure is quoted. [GAP: benchmark source.] Any future comparison must quote its source and year from a resolved knowledge-base entry — never a bare figure.

**Occupational injuries:** the source log records 12 recordable injuries in the period (aggregated; sub-categories suppressed at source). Recordable injuries belong to the occupational TRIR/LTIFR/DART family, **not** the API RP 754 PSE pyramid, and are excluded from every count and rate above. Route that dataset to the `incident-rate-calculator` workstream (action A8), preserving the aggregation and secondary suppression already applied.
